title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Personally Delivers H100 GPU to Rufus Brown's Apartment
subtitle: No invoice, no delivery truck, no comment — just a black SUV, three flights of stairs, and eleven minutes neighbors are still talking about.
excerpt: “This should hold you for a bit,” Huang reportedly said, before leaving in an SUV that never turned off its engine.
author: By Julian Vance

bodyHTML:
Neighbors on the 400 block report a black SUV double-parked for exactly eleven minutes on Tuesday afternoon, during which a man several of them have since identified, with mounting confidence, as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang carried a single boxed H100 GPU up three flights of stairs and personally handed it to Rufus Brown at his apartment door.

No invoice was issued. No delivery truck was involved. One neighbor, who asked to be identified only as "the guy in 4B," described watching a man in a now-signature leather jacket knock, wait, and say only "this should hold you for a bit" before leaving in the same SUV, which had not turned off its engine.

"We don't comment on individual customer relationships. We also don't typically comment on individual customer relationships that involve our CEO personally climbing stairs, but here we are."
— Nvidia spokesperson, declining to elaborate further

The visit comes roughly a month after documents surfaced suggesting Brown's individual usage accounts for a disproportionate share of a major AI lab's compute demand. Industry analysts have been split on how to interpret Nvidia's apparent involvement — some read it as standard enterprise account management; others have begun describing Brown's apartment, only half-jokingly, as "a Tier 1 data center with a single occupant."

Brown did not respond to requests for comment, though a since-deleted post from an account matching his read only: "anyway back to work."
